SK1092 Use a tuple literal instead of constructing a Tuple

A local is initialized with new Tuple<…>(…) or Tuple.Create(…) and is only ever read element by element, so a tuple literal is the same value without the allocation.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, review it
Language version floorC# 7.0
Since2.0

Why

(string name, int age) is a value type, allocates nothing, and carries element names the reference Tuple has no room for. This is squarely the SK1xxx premise: Tuple predates ValueTuple by six years, so a model writes the older dialect because the older dialect is most of what it has read.

Example

Instead of:

var pair = new Tuple<int, string>(1, "a");
Use(pair.Item1, pair.Item2);

Write:

var pair = (1, "a");
Use(pair.Item1, pair.Item2);

When it does not fire

⚠ `System.Tuple<…>` is a class and `System.ValueTuple<…>` is a struct, so the rewrite changes nullability, equality and allocation all at once — and Item1-style member access works on both, which means the shape alone proves nothing. The rule therefore does not report a Tuple construction anywhere it might escape: it reports only a local declaration, and only when every reference to that local in the enclosing member is a t.ItemN read. A local that is returned, passed as an argument, assigned to anything, compared with == (identity on Tuple, structural on ValueTuple), tested with is, cast, or reassigned is left alone, because each of those is a place where the difference between the two types is observable. ⚠ Arity 2 to 7 only. Tuple<T> has no literal form — (x) is a parenthesized expression — and the eighth element is TRest, whose nesting the fix does not reproduce. ⚠ The written type arguments are what the fix reuses, not a display string derived from the symbol: Tuple<int, string> becomes (int, string) textually, so a type spelled with a using alias or a name only reachable from this file keeps compiling. A named argument is declined, because a tuple literal cannot carry the argument names Tuple.Create accepts. ⚠ System.ValueTuple2 must exist in the compilation; on a target framework that predates it the fix would not compile. ⚠ fixIsSafe is false` and stays false even under all of the above: the constraints prove the value does not escape this declaration, and reviewing a type change from a class to a struct is cheap next to being wrong about it.
